title: Sponsor Services Training Note: Invoice Disputes under the PBM Services Agreement
content:
**The rule.** The plan sponsor may dispute an invoice under its PBM Services Agreement no later than the arrangement's dispute window, in calendar days, after the invoice date, the invoice date being day zero; a timely dispute is resolved within the arrangement's dispute resolution period, and an upheld dispute is credited as a billing error credit memo against that invoice. A late dispute is not accepted, and the disputed amount stays due while the dispute is open.

## Questions answered by the rule

**From which date is the window counted?**
From the invoice date of the invoice being disputed, as shown on that invoice's record. The invoice date is day zero; the next calendar day is day 1.

**Is the last day of the window still in time?**
Yes. A dispute raised on the day whose number equals the dispute window is in time; a dispute raised on any later day is late.

**What happens to a late dispute?**
It is not accepted.

**Does an open dispute pause payment of the invoice?**
No. The disputed amount stays due while the dispute is open.

**How long does resolution take?**
A timely dispute is resolved within the arrangement's dispute resolution period, in calendar days.

**What does an upheld dispute produce?**
A credit memo for a billing error, applied against the disputed invoice.

## Boundary days (hypothetical window of 30 calendar days)

| Day the dispute is raised, counted from the invoice date | In time |
|---|---|
| Day 0 (the invoice date) | Yes |
| Day 29 | Yes |
| Day 30 | Yes — the last day of the window |
| Day 31 | No — not accepted |

## A worked case (hypothetical)

An invoice dated on day 0 is disputed on day 30 under a 30-day window: the dispute is timely and is resolved within the resolution period. Meanwhile the full invoice amount, including the disputed part, remains due on its due date. If the dispute is upheld, the billing error is credited as a credit memo against that same invoice. Had the same dispute been raised on day 31, it would not have been accepted.
